synopsis: ISO publishes international standards central to heavy off-road validation, including the collision-warning and avoidance framework of ISO 21815-1, ISO 21815-3, ISO 16001 and the ISO 19014 functional-safety series; standards acquire legal significance through incorporation, harmonisation or designation, contracts, procurement, or a chosen state-of-the-art demonstration route [f15017, f7403, f2144]. As of 1 October 2026, published ISO 19014 Parts 1–4 were respectively dated 2018, 2022, 2018 and 2020, and Part 5 was ISO/TS 19014-5:2021; second editions of Parts 2 and 5 and ISO 21815-4 on swing and rotation were under publication in October 2026, so the program should re-baseline on editions actually published [f2315, f2319, f2322, f2325, f2328, f6285, f7730, f11914]. ISO permits speed reduction, stopping or motion inhibition rather than prescribing one response, and its distance budget begins at detection, making reduced reliable detection range a margin that no brake model can recover [f3622, f6584, f13999]. No universal target dimensions, test counts, sufficient hours or encounters, or rule validating an entire machine family from N representative machines was found; acceptance values need a normative clause before being called ISO-mandated, and safety-relevant variants need confirmation evidence [f5410, f5447, f6683, f2636, f14457]. ISO scenario methods help establish representative virtual-test coverage, while the on-road Euro NCAP 2026 protocol requires physical-test correlation using ISO-based scores before virtual results count [f8031, f14718]. Passing conformity assessment, ISO tests and functional-safety verification nevertheless does not guarantee mine operating authorisation [f2930].
